step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Biopharma's genomic data ingestion and curation pipeline. Raw genomic sequencing data (ATCGs) is ingested into ad-hoc EC2 instances and written directly to Amazon FSx storage. Software environments and pipelines defined on EC2 are built into versioned container images and pushed to Amazon ECR. Amazon EKS pulls these versioned container images from ECR to execute curation workloads at scale. Amazon FSx is mounted onto the EKS worker nodes to feed raw genomic input data into the curation tasks. Finally, the processed matrix outputs generated by EKS are written to the S3-based Data Lake for analysis. The human stick figure actor representing end-user data scientists is pruned per Rule 5 as it is a downstream consumer rather than an active system entry point.

nodes.notes: Private container registry storing versioned pipeline container images for reproducible processing.
